ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $l_{1}\colon y=-x-3$ intersects with the line $l_{2}$ passing through the point $A(0,3)$ at point $C(m,1)$, and intersects with the y-axis at point $B$. Find the analytical expression of the line $l_{2}$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Substitute C($m$,1) into $y=-x-3$ to get $-m-3=1$,\\
$\therefore m=-4$,\\
$\therefore$ C($-4$,1). Let the equation of line $l_{2}$ be $y=kx+b$. Substituting A(0,3) and C($-4$,1) into it, we get
\[
\begin{cases}
b=3, \\
-4k+b=1,
\end{cases}
\]
which, upon solving, gives
\[
\begin{cases}
k=\frac{1}{2}, \\
b=3,
\end{cases}
\]
$\therefore$ The equation of line $l_{2}$ is $\boxed{y=\frac{1}{2}x+3}$;
